# Netflix: the valuation question is cash content economics

Research cutoff: **19 October 2026**. Capital/discount anchor: **30 June 2026**. USD amounts below are billions unless noted.

**Tomorrow's Q3 release is pending.** The retained [14 September issuer announcement](https://ir.netflix.net/investor-news-and-events/financial-releases/press-release-details/2026/Netflix-to-Announce-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) schedules results for 20 October 2026, approximately 1:01 p.m. Pacific. Its actual announcement text is archived and hash-checked; the older dynamic event-page shell is not date evidence. Do not call this a Q3-updated valuation.

## Bottom line

The ten-year evidence supports building an editable FCFF model. It does not support presenting a current October target from June cash and shares. The operating scenarios give approximately **$107.7bn bear / $254.0bn base / $447.9bn bull** in conditional June operating value. Their breadth is intentional: long-term revenue, margins, content cash timing and discount rates are assumptions, not probabilities or management promises.

A separately selected illustrative claim policy allocates approximately **$23.53 / $57.87 / $103.16 per June-equivalent share**. The default output remains unselected. These amounts reserve operating liquidity, existing options including assumed time value, an assumed multiplier of outstanding RSUs/PSUs, and explicitly assumed unresolved claims. They are not current price targets, exact historical fair values, or upside estimates.

## Business and historical economics

Netflix sells recurring entertainment access; advertising and other monetization complement membership revenue. Revenue depends on the number and mix of paying households, prices, plan changes, advertising yield and exchange rates. Four geographic revenue disclosures are not separately reported profit centers. A global content library creates scale benefits, but content production is a recurrent operating investment rather than an asset that can stop being replenished. [FY2025 10-K, Business and revenue note](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm)

| Fiscal year | Revenue | EBIT | EBIT margin | CFO less PPE | Content cash / amortization |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | 8.831 | 0.380 | 4.3% | -1.582 | 1.44x |
| 2017 | 11.693 | 0.839 | 7.2% | -1.959 | 1.44x |
| 2018 | 15.794 | 1.605 | 10.2% | -2.854 | 1.60x |
| 2019 | 20.156 | 2.604 | 12.9% | -3.140 | 1.59x |
| 2020 | 24.996 | 4.585 | 18.3% | 1.929 | 1.16x |
| 2021 | 29.698 | 6.195 | 20.9% | -0.132 | 1.43x |
| 2022 | 31.616 | 5.633 | 17.8% | 1.619 | 1.19x |
| 2023 | 33.723 | 6.954 | 20.6% | 6.926 | 0.93x |
| 2024 | 39.001 | 10.418 | 26.7% | 6.922 | 1.11x |
| 2025 | 45.183 | 13.327 | 29.5% | 9.461 | 1.08x |

The historical CSV and field provenance are the reproducible source of these figures. CFO less PPE is not issuer-defined historical FCF, FCFF, acquisition-inclusive cash flow, or a measure net of the economic cost of SBC. For example FY2021 issuer FCF was -$158.894m after an additional $26.919m investing-asset outflow; the table intentionally shows the narrower -$131.975m CFO-less-PPE figure. Content ratios cover the streaming/content cash-flow rows; separately disclosed historical DVD investment is retained separately. The old DVD business, 2019 lease-accounting change, pandemic production disruption and 2023 strikes limit simple trend extrapolation. [FY2018 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528019000043/form10k_q418.htm), [FY2021 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528022000036/nflx-20211231.htm), [FY2023 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528024000030/nflx-20231231.htm)

## The content cash bridge

Cash content payments = negative of the signed additions-to-content-assets and content-liability-change rows. In 2025 that is $17.707bn, against $16.422bn amortization. In H1 2026 it is $9.911bn against $8.529bn amortization. Cash purchases are already inside operating cash flow. Adding content amortization back without subtracting those cash payments materially overstates distributable cash. [FY2025 cash-flow statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm), [H1 2026 cash-flow statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm)

The model starts from EBIT and calculates:

    FCFF = EBIT - operating cash tax + content amortization - cash content payments
           + noncontent D&A - PPE purchases - noncontent operating investment

Existing content liabilities are not deducted again as financial debt. Opening commitments remain economically relevant: the June filing reports $25.107bn total content obligations, including $11.940bn due within twelve months. An additional unknown-title range is disclosed but does not represent a complete forecast of future investment. The editable model requires H2 2026 cash content plus an explicitly selected fraction of FY2027 cash content to cover the disclosed $11,939.734m due in the next twelve months. The illustration assumes 50% of FY2027 cash falls in H1: bear/base/bull coverage is $21,984.782m / $20,829.142m / $20,071.208m. Both input validation and direct allocation withhold insufficient coverage; even assigning all FY2027 spending to H1 cannot rescue an insufficient annual amount. Passing is only a necessary aggregate capacity condition. It does not prove title-specific payment dates, gross-versus-net incentive timing, intrayear liquidity or new-commitment coverage. Content liabilities are still not deducted again as debt. [June 10-Q, commitments and liquidity](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm)

## Current-period normalization

H1 revenue was $24.810bn and EBIT $8.150bn. The $2.8bn WBD termination receipt sits below EBIT; it must not become recurring operating cash generation. June cash already includes the receipt, so it is never added again to the equity bridge. The package does not assert an exact after-tax recurring-income adjustment, because a matched tax/cash normalization was not separately established. [June 10-Q, acquisition note](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm)

July guidance was FY2026 revenue $51.0–51.4bn, 31.5% operating margin, approximately $12.5bn CFO-minus-PPE FCF, roughly $3bn advertising revenue and cash content/amortization around 1.1x. The model uses the revenue midpoint and operating-margin guidance for its base 2026 setup. Guidance FCF is not simply relabeled normalized FCFF. [16 July shareholder letter](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000211/ex991_q226.htm)

## What is assumed

- H2 2026 is a dated stub, obtained by subtracting reported H1 operating and investment amounts from separately assumed full-year amounts. Forecast taxes are applied to H2 EBIT, not derived by subtracting the termination-fee-distorted H1 tax provision.
- Nine full forecast years follow, 2027–2035. Base annual revenue growth fades from 11% to 3.5%; base EBIT margin reaches 35%. Bear and bull paths are independently stated, editable assumptions.
- Cash taxes are 25%/21%/18% in bear/base/bull. This avoids perpetually extrapolating unusually low book-tax rates or SBC tax benefits. These are assumptions, not claims about statutory tax law.
- Base amortization is assumed at $18bn in FY2026, then explicit percentages of revenue. Base cash content/amortization falls from 1.10x toward 1.04x. Capex, noncontent D&A and working capital remain separately visible.
- WACC is 10.5%/9%/8%, terminal growth 2%/2.5%/3%, and incremental terminal ROIC 12%/15%/20%. These are subjective nominal-USD required-return scenarios, not a current market-estimated WACC.
- Terminal net reinvestment is the greater of content/PPE/working-capital needs and NOPAT × growth / incremental ROIC. The two are not added together. Terminal taxes never disappear.
- Terminal PV represents about 51.1%/59.5%/67.9% of EV. A large share of value remains dependent on economics beyond the explicit forecast.

## Capital and allocation

At June 30, cash plus short-term investments were $9.128bn, excluding restricted cash. Debt is separately shown at $14.309bn carrying amount, approximately $14.372bn face value and $14.605bn fair value. The example selects face value. Operating leases stay inside operating expenses and are not deducted a second time. [June 10-Q, balance sheet, debt and lease notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm)

The exact reported June share count is **4,163,939,676**, versus **4,279,776,000 H1 diluted weighted-average EPS shares**. Existing options are **123,891,603**, all vested/exercisable, at a $39.21 weighted-average strike. Unvested RSU/PSU rollforward units are **2,012,512**; this is not an established legal maximum payout. All historical shares are normalized for the November 2025 ten-for-one split, once only. [June equity/EPS notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm), [FY2025 split disclosure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm)

The illustrative policy reserves $3bn operating cash, applies a 2x award-unit multiplier, and uses a weighted-strike Black-Scholes option proxy with assumed 35% volatility, 4.5-year remaining term and 4% risk-free rate. It solves common value and option value together; it does not add hypothetical exercise cash again. This is an approximation with materially different possible grant-level outcomes.

The June cash-flow discussion reports **$729m of non-routine Brazil non-income-tax assessment payments already made in H1 for prior periods**. They already reduced June cash. The earlier FY2025 expectation of roughly $700m deposits must not be deducted or paid again after June. The corrected versions remove that duplicated v1 reserve. No recovery asset is added. The illustration deliberately assumes **zero additional Brazil exposure beyond the paid amount**; that is an assumption, not verification that further exposure is absent. It retains $566m for income-tax uncertainty using the stale FY2025 gross unrecognized-benefit amount as an explicit assumption, plus $250m other claims. [June liquidity discussion](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm), [FY2025 tax and contingency notes](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm)

**Financing hedges are separate from operating FX.** June interest-rate derivative assets of $0.236m current and $1.124m noncurrent, less a $14.934m liability, give a **$13.574m net financing liability**. The illustration reserves that amount separately from the $14,372m face principal. It does not also deduct the approximately negative $14m debt carrying-basis adjustment. June financing FX fair-value-hedge notional is $2,934.991m; its net fair value is not separately identifiable in the disclosed table, which combines designated operating and financing FX fair values. The example explicitly assumes a $100m financing FX closeout reserve, rather than labeling it reported, deducting notional or adding all gross derivatives. Operating cash-flow FX hedges remain in revenue/cost forecasts, with no separate opening net asset credited. [June Notes 7 and 8](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm)

The matching cash scenario hypothetically closes financing hedges on July 1 at those separately stated values, pays total separate claims of **$929.574m in H2**, and uses unhedged 4.9% interest and constant June FX thereafter. This is an explicit conditional funding convention, not evidence that closeout occurred or a full market-value debt/hedge appraisal. Carrying or standalone market debt values cannot be substituted into this face-principal convention without a new matched implementation.

**Existing unvested awards versus future grants:** core GAAP-like EBIT includes compensation expense. To avoid separately allocating existing RSU/PSU units while also charging their remaining vesting expense, allocation requires a ten-period schedule of that expense embedded in the forecast. The illustration assumes $25m in H2 2026, $25m in 2027, $10m in 2028 and explicitly zero thereafter. It adds only the after-tax PV of that schedule to the core EV before allocating existing awards: approximately $39.81m / $42.63m / $44.74m in bear/base/bull. There is no terminal or broad SBC addback. Future-grant cash-replacement compensation remains charged and excludes the existing-award expense removed by this adjustment. All June options are already vested. The $60m schedule is an analyst assumption, not a verified June remaining-cost balance; the FY2025 filing's $47m unrecognized RSU/PSU cost over 1.53 years is dated context. V3 requires the entire schedule to reconcile exactly to the selected total remaining expense. Its example recognition horizon is December 31, 2028. No June-existing expense may be recognized beyond June 30, 2029 under the implemented unmodified-award convention, reflecting disclosed three-year RSU vesting and one-to-three-year PSU performance periods. An amount assigned to the last partial year must be recognized by the selected date; year-end PV remains a conservative annual timing approximation. Tax effects use the assumed operating rate without a separate excess-tax-benefit credit. [June awards](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm), [FY2025 compensation disclosure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm)

### V3 expense guardrails

V2's named $60m schedule passed independent arithmetic review, but arbitrary edits could remove more expense than existed or push June-existing awards into 2035. V3 closes that admission gap with **joint** limits:

- Pre-adjustment operating costs equal revenue less EBIT. Content amortization and noncontent D&A are retained first; the same components cannot be removed as award compensation.
- The illustration retains **1.1% of revenue for future-grant cash-replacement compensation and 20% for other cash operating costs**, for H2 2026, every full forecast year and terminal 2036. These are explicit components already embedded in EBIT, never additional FCFF deductions. Both schedules are editable, but this restricted convention requires future-grant compensation to remain at least FY2025 total SBC/revenue, **0.815459%**, and requires other cash costs to remain positive. That historical-intensity floor is a deliberate forward-cost assumption, not a statement of reported future pay. A lower-compensation thesis needs a separately supported convention.
- Existing-award expense must fit what remains after those retained costs, as well as its own aggregate budget and recognition horizon. For base H2, the $18,411.912m total costs contain $9,470.791m content amortization and $250.895m noncontent D&A. After the example's $290.293m future-grant compensation and $5,278.061m other cash-cost floors, only $3,121.872m remains available for all other unallocated costs and the existing-award adjustment. The $25m adjustment fits; a $10,000m adjustment does not.
- The budget also cannot exceed the implemented **source-context reference envelope of approximately $150.2547m**: dated FY2025 $47m plus H1 grants of 1.245383m units times $82.91 weighted grant-date value. This restriction requires the explicit assumption that there are no unmodeled positive cost modifications or other additions. It intentionally does not subtract unknown H1 recognition or grants linked to prior-period PSU settlement. It is an analytical admission limit, **not a verified June unrecognized-cost balance or legal/grant-level ceiling**. Larger amounts require a new supported reconciliation rather than an unchecked override.

The source grant table itself includes 264,300 PSUs granted and 528,600 vested from a prior performance period and settled in Q1; this is why multiplying all H1 grants cannot establish exact remaining expense. The disclosed weighted prices and opening unrecognized amount are also rounded. Missing assumptions withhold allocation, while inconsistent or impossible selected policies are rejected. The named v2/v3 arithmetic remains unchanged. [June Note 10](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000212/nflx-20260630.htm), [FY2025 stock compensation](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000034/nflx-20251231.htm)

The annual funding test retains FCFF, pays the June debt-maturity schedule using fixed June FX, assumes a 4.9% interest proxy and no future buybacks, dividends, acquisitions or refinancing. It is a funding-capacity stress, **not a forecast bank balance**. Large repurchase authorizations are discretionary and not assumed share reductions.

## The known July financing is paired, not a permanent blocker

On July 22, Netflix issued $1bn face value of 5.25% notes due 2036. The underwriters paid 98.855% of principal: $988.55m before other issuer expenses. Thus this isolated event adds **$11.45m net debt before other expenses**, rather than subtracting $1bn from equity without the cash proceeds. Intended repayment of November 2026 notes is not treated as a completed pre-October repayment. [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000119312526312575/d171951d8k.htm), [underwriting agreement §2(a)](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000119312526312575/d171951dex11.htm)

The roll-forward template requires operating cash, PPE/acquisition uses, buybacks and shares, exercises and proceeds, other financing/FX and current awards. Missing entries stay null. A completed capital ledger would still require removing elapsed FCFF and updating the remaining forecast before calling the result an October valuation.

## What can change the answer

1. Pricing, paid-sharing or advertising growth may fail to sustain the assumed revenue/margin paths; competitive entertainment has low switching barriers.
2. Weaker content returns or accelerated amortization can damage margins while production cash remains committed. Slower cash spending can instead temporarily flatter FCF.
3. Local taxes, regulation, content quotas, currency movements and incentive-collection timing can change cash conversion. Historical effective tax rates are poor standalone forecasts.
4. Live programming, games, new formats and acquisitions may require more investment than the organic cases allow.
5. Ongoing repurchases and award exercises make June shares stale for a current quote. Option time value, maximum PSU rights, taxes and derivative timing remain allocation uncertainties.
6. Q3 results due October 20 may materially change both operations and capital. Refresh the package after publication, preserving this snapshot.

## Admission

Author tests cover source-table comparisons, historical transforms, independent annual/terminal arithmetic, paid-claim reconciliation, financing-hedge matching, existing-award expense allocation, the independent low-content counterexample and exact commitment boundary, funding gates, null/bool/nonfinite rejection and the paired financing event. V1 remains preserved but its equity allocation and unrestricted editable model were not admitted by independent review. Independent v2 review closed the original four source/model findings and verified its named policy arithmetic, but withheld unrestricted award-expense edits. V3 adds budget, recognition-horizon and retained-cost constraints with realistic boundary tests and requires its own targeted review. They are not an audit opinion. Admit history and conditional scenarios only after separate independent review. No current target, current upside, or exact-current-share claim is approved by this package.
